**Relevant information:** Item 1 is the only one on this topic. It summarizes the "Experimental Results" section of the "To Adapt or Not to Adapt? Real-Time Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation" submission. It says the proposed framework achieved "an average improvement in framerate of approximately 20% when using the Hardware-Aware Modular Training (HAMT) agent and a further improvement of approximately 4x with the addition of the Active Training Modulation system."

**Reasoning:** The question asks about the average framerate improvement from the HAMT agent alone. The 4x figure is a further improvement from adding Active Training Modulation, so it does not answer the question.

**Answer:** The HAMT agent gave an average framerate improvement of approximately 20%.

**Relevant information:**

Real-Time Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation" submission, I said the HAMLET framework gave an average framerate improvement of **approximately 20%** with the Hardware-Aware Modular Training (HAMT) agent.
- That same summary said adding the Active Training Modulation system gave a further improvement of about 4x.
- No later item updates or replaces that figure.

**Reasoning:**
The question asks only about the HAMT agent. The 20% figure applies to HAMT alone. The 4x figure is a separate, additional gain from Active Training Modulation.

**Answer:**
Using the HAMT agent gave an average framerate improvement of **approximately 20%**. Adding Active Training Modulation on top raised it by roughly a further 4x.
